description: A physics-based LFO: particles orbit four attractors, and their positions and velocities come out as control voltages

params.text: Removes the particle added most recently
Turns the random drifting of the attractors on and off
Sets the gravity of all four attractors, 1 to 50
Turns that coloured attractor on and off
Scales the gravity of that coloured attractor, -1 to +2, negative settings pushing particles away

inputs.text: A trigger turns the random drifting of the attractors on and off
Multiplies the gravity set by the G knob by two to the power of the voltage

outputs.text: Carries the horizontal position of each particle, -5V at the left edge to +5V at the right, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the vertical position of each particle, -5V at the bottom to +5V at the top, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the horizontal position of each particle inverted, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the vertical position of each particle inverted, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the horizontal velocity of each particle, -5V to +5V, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the vertical velocity of each particle, -5V to +5V, one polyphonic channel per particle
Carries the average of the horizontal positions of all the particles as a single voltage
Carries the average of the vertical positions of all the particles as a single voltage
Carries the largest horizontal position among the particles as a single voltage
Carries the largest vertical position among the particles as a single voltage
Carries the smallest horizontal position among the particles as a single voltage
Carries the smallest vertical position among the particles as a single voltage

notes: click an attractor to drag it, and click elsewhere in the display to add a particle
the display comes up with two particles in it, and clicking anywhere but on an attractor adds another.
menu: Polyphony channels — sets how many particles the poly outputs carry, Monophonic or 1 to 16
Particle trails — draws no trail, a white trail, or one shifted towards red and blue by the speed of the particle
Particle boundaries — on bounces particles off the edges of the display; off lets them leave it
